Krach Kazan crossed the field in a few quick strides to where the empress was bound to a tree, stepping easily among the bodies of the bandits he had slain. In a single slash, he released her bonds. She threw herself on him, crying into his barrel chest, which was wrapped in the colors of the great houses.

"You have the gratitude of the empire," she sobbed. "Anything, anything you want—you'll have it!"

"There's only one thing I want," he said, pulling away so they could look eye to eye. "And it isn't jade or jewels or fancy titles. It's for the sons and daughters of Echovald to wake up tomorrow and breathe free. Without freedom, nothing else matters, because a free man owns the most valuable thing in the world—himself."

Captain Sylvour Denwatcher,

Firstly I hope you are well, old friend. I know these days are dire.  
  
I will keep this brief. I am writing to inquire about one of your inmates. A certain...suave sylvari, if I'm to believe the rumors. I've done my research, and I see that he's led a tumultuous and storied life so far: involuntary test subject, Consortium cartographer and project team leader, Molten Facility liberator, and corporate saboteur. For all his struggles, he's developed something of a reputation, even in the quieter halls of Divinity's Reach. And as it turns out, I have use for a man of his particular "prestige" and skillset.  
  
There are places I cannot move through without notice and things I cannot do from my current station without drawing unwanted attention, so I've learned to delegate more effectively. In this case, he would serve as an...extension of the Shining Blade and the Krytan crown—under my express supervision, of course. If you think he'd be at all cooperative, I am interested in purchasing his billet.  
  
Thank you for your time,  
  
Countess Anise, Exemplar of the Shining Blade

strings.en:
There's nothing like the sand of an ancient beach between your toes to feel the exhilaration of potential this untapped land has to offer us. With Vloxx, Sebb, and Kuda as the tip of our lance, we will make Castora ours.  

I'm being sent with a patrol to scout the coast. There's a whole fleet's worth of wrecked ships from the outer rocks up to the beach—ours included, now. Here's hoping there's survivors we can poke and prod for answers about this place. It's anyone's guess as to which way the expedition should be headed.  

***

I almost miss the Aetherblades. The freebooters are a dim bunch, but they have their uses. Still, I'm not trusting those sloshed bookahs with my lab equipment; I'll use the golems for that.

It's been some weeks since we landed, and we finally established a proper base in the forest. The levels of ambient magic here are unbelievable. There must be some deeper source in these parts that ultimately went untouched by the Elder Dragons. Whatever the original seer residents did to obscure this place from the rest of Tyria was no small feat.  

My lab krewe leader, Zenna, wastes most of her day placating the anxieties of one of her subordinates, a tag-a-long from her college days. Regardless, they're holding our team back. If things don't improve soon, I'm requesting a transfer.  

***

I've been doing delicate work as of late, rewiring and overriding some these "stewards" my colleagues have hauled in to Supra Fortis from around the Forge. Arty won't let me near the big one. His funeral, I guess. His engineering work is as slipshod as the scrap heap he has for a brain; it'd be nice if Kuda upgraded it.  

***

Our new director has need of me for Project Gamma tomorrow. She brought up my medical files the other day and said I was an ideal fit for the project. Hand picked by the new director! I can hardly believe it. I haven't been sleeping well since we set up station down here in the ruins beneath the temple—something about the damp air—but maybe the thought of tomorrow's events will be just the motivation my mind needs to find rest.
